Minority Looms as Quebec Provincial Election Continues 
The approval ratings are practically the same for Premier Christine
Fréchette and PQ leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon. 
Vancouver, BC [September 15, 2026] – Voters in Quebec appear
headed to the closest provincial election since 2012, a new
Research Co. poll has found.
In the online survey of a representative sample of Quebecers, 28%
of decided voters would support the Parti Québécois (PQ), while
23% would back the governing Coalition Avenir Québec (CAQ)
and 22% would cast a ballot for a Liberal Party of Quebec
candidate.
Support is lower for the Conservative Party of Quebec (16%) and
Québec solidaire (10%).
The PQ holds the upper hand in the Quebec City Metropolitan
Area with 29%, followed by the Conservatives with 23% and the
CAQ with 21%. In the Montreal Metropolitan Area, the PQ and the
Liberals are tied at 25%, with the CAQ at 21%. In the rest of the
province, the PQ is two-points ahead of the CAQ (30% to 28%).
“At this point in the 2022 electoral campaign, the CAQ was the
only party garnering the support of more than one-in-five decided
voters,” says Mario Canseco, President of Research Co. “This year,
three parties meet the same threshold.”
Only in two of the seven provincial elections held in this century in
Quebec has a party finished in first place with about a third of all
cast ballots: the Liberals in 2007 (33%) and the PQ in 2012 (32%).
Both elections resulted in minority governments.
More than two-in-five Quebecers approve of the performance of
PQ leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon (45%) and Premier and
Coalition Avenir Québec leader Christine Fréchette (45%). The
rating is lower for Liberal leader Charles Millard (37%), Québec
solidaire co-spokesperson Ruba Ghazal (34%) and Conservative
leader Éric Duhaime (31%).
Fréchette has a four-point lead over Plamondon on the “Best
Premier” question (25% to 21%), with Duhaime and Millard tied at
11% and Ghazal at 7%.
Similar proportions of Quebecers say their opinion of Fréchette has
improved (23%) or worsened (25%) since the start of the
campaign for a momentum score of -2. The results on this question
are also negative for Ghazal (-5), Duhaime (-7), Plamondon (-10)
and Millard (-14).

Health care (28%) and housing, poverty and homelessness (also
28%) are tied when Quebecers ponder the most important issue
facing the province. The economy and jobs is third with 23 per
cent, followed by government accountability (5%), the
environment (3%), crime and public safety (also 3%) and
education (also 3%).
When asked which of the five party leaders is best suited to
manage specific issues, Fréchette is ahead of Plamondon on
government accountability (24% to 20%), the economy and jobs
(23% to 18%), health care (22% to 18%), education (21% to 19%),
housing, poverty and homelessness (20% to 17%) and crime and
public safety (20% to 18%).
Fréchette is two-points ahead of Duhaime on energy and
pipelines (19% to 17%), while Plamondon has a sizeable lead on
national unity and separation over Fréchette (27% to 16%). Ghazal
and Fréchette are virtually tied on the environment (20% and 19%
respectively).
